title: How Exact works
description: A visual guide to Contract, TypeScript, Rust and rightui, with a simple comparison to Expo.

sections.title: From your code to the screen
sections.text:
Exact is the complete system. Contract describes the interface. TypeScript or Rust supplies your data.

1. **You write:** Contract describes screens, styles, state and actions. rightui provides reusable Contract components.
2. **Exact builds:** the compiler checks your interface and creates a compact plan describing what to show and how to respond.
3. **Exact runs:** the runtime executes that plan. The host displays the result using the browser DOM and CSS on Web, UIKit on iOS or AppKit on macOS.

**Data at runtime:** Exact asks your TypeScript or Rust data module for API calls, storage and business logic, checks the reply and updates the UI.

You can build with **Contract + TypeScript without writing Rust**. Rust also powers parts of Exact internally; that does not make it a language you must write. Web, iOS and macOS are rightui targets; see the [compatibility table](/docs/compatibility) for checks completed on each platform.

sections.title: Inside the runtime
sections.text:
| Layer | Job |
| --- | --- |
| Runner | Handles events, state changes and requests to the data module. |
| Kernel | Calculates sizes and positions on native platforms. On the web, the browser uses CSS for layout. |
| Host | Displays the result with DOM, UIKit or AppKit. |

[Exact architecture](https://github.com/expo/exact/blob/53426cf02bf986a5e781abc4f953d79989c6dc05/README.md#how-it-works)

sections.title: Coming from Expo?
sections.text:
Expo is a framework built around React Native. Exact provides its own UI language, compiler and runtime. These are useful points of comparison, not interchangeable packages.

| Role | Expo / React Native | Exact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interface | React components in JSX / TSX | Components in Contract |
| UI state | React and JavaScript | Contract state and actions |
| Data logic | Usually JavaScript / TypeScript | TypeScript or Rust |
| UI library | React / React Native components | rightui Contract components |

React components cannot be imported as Contract components. rightui is written for Exact. [About the Expo framework](https://docs.expo.dev/get-started/create-a-project/)

sections.title: One example: load products
sections.text:
Imagine a Load products button in your app.

1. **Contract + rightui:** pressing the button triggers a Contract action. The UI can show a loading state.
2. **TypeScript or Rust:** the data module calls your API and returns product records.
3. **Exact runtime + Contract:** Exact checks the reply against the declared shape. Contract renders the products and the host displays the result.

A local interaction, like opening a menu, can stay entirely in Contract. A data request is needed only when the action needs your data module.

sections.title: Start with Contract + TypeScript
sections.text:
Use rightui for the components and app.ts for your data. Choose Rust when your project needs a Rust data source; the UI still stays in Contract.

Continue with [Installation](/docs/installation), the [TypeScript example](/docs/installation/typescript) or [Rust integration](/docs/installation/rust).

title: Installation
description: Add rightui components to your Exact app. Current release: {{UI_VERSION}} (beta).

sections.title: Install with your AI agent
sections.text: Copy this prompt into any coding agent. It will check your project, install rightui and add a working component.
sections.code:
Add rightui to this project using the official @rightui/ui npm package.

Read https://rightui.dev/docs/installation.md and https://rightui.dev/llms.txt first. Follow this repository's instructions and preserve existing features, styling and uncommitted changes.

1. Inspect the project. rightui provides Exact Contract components for web, iOS and macOS. Find the Exact app, its package.json, app.contract and pinned SDK. If this is not an Exact project, explain that rightui cannot be imported as React, React Native or Vue components, and ask before creating an Exact app or migrating anything.

2. Install @rightui/ui@{{UI_VERSION}} as an exact dependency in the consuming app, using the project's package manager. With Bun: bun add --exact @rightui/ui@{{UI_VERSION}}. Use the published npm package; do not substitute a local checkout, Git dependency or an invented adapter. Keep the lockfile in sync. Check the documented Exact compatibility and report any mismatch before changing the SDK.

3. Follow the font setup in the installation guide: copy Geist.ttf, Geist-Italic.ttf, Newsreader.ttf, Newsreader-Italic.ttf, OFL.txt, OFL-Italic.txt and OFL-Newsreader.txt from the package into the app's assets/fonts directory, then register Geist and Newsreader in Contract if it is not already configured. Preserve an intentional existing typeface. Add "rightui-font" to the top-level app.json data allowlist, preserving existing entries. Add uiFont = "theme" and uiWeights = defaultFontWeights() to the root component’s provide block (merge with its existing provide block). For runtime switching, provide a state choosing "sans", "serif" or "mono" instead.

If adding a code block, also install the root clipboard controller from the guide.

4. Import components with Contract syntax, for example: use Button from "@rightui/ui". Add a small working interaction to the appropriate existing screen using the documented props. Keep UI state and actions in Contract; keep existing TypeScript or Rust data logic in its data module. Do not replace the app with a starter template.

5. Run the project's build and relevant tests, then check the new interaction and responsive layout. Report the files changed, package version and checks actually completed. Distinguish web checks from native device validation, and list any remaining blockers.

sections.title: Before you start
sections.text: Use an Exact app and Bun 1.4.2. This beta is tested with [expo/exact revision 53426cf](https://github.com/expo/exact/tree/53426cf02bf986a5e781abc4f953d79989c6dc05). If you are new to Exact, follow its [setup guide](https://github.com/expo/exact/blob/53426cf02bf986a5e781abc4f953d79989c6dc05/README.md) and create an app first. Run the following commands from your app directory. For a visual introduction to the layers, read [How Exact works](/docs/how-exact-works).

sections.title: Install the package
sections.text: Install the shared component package once. Choose the package manager you use in your project. Pin the version while rightui is in beta.

sections.title: Allow the font marker
sections.text: Add rightui-font to the top-level data allowlist in app.json. Merge it with existing entries. RightUI uses this marker to identify text that follows the body typeface.

sections.title: Add the typeface
sections.text: Copy the bundled Geist and Newsreader families with their licenses. Declare their regular and italic faces at the top of app.contract, as shown in the next step.
sections.code:
mkdir -p assets/fonts
cp node_modules/@rightui/ui/assets/fonts/Geist.ttf assets/fonts/
cp node_modules/@rightui/ui/assets/fonts/Geist-Italic.ttf assets/fonts/
cp node_modules/@rightui/ui/assets/fonts/OFL.txt assets/fonts/
cp node_modules/@rightui/ui/assets/fonts/OFL-Italic.txt assets/fonts/
cp node_modules/@rightui/ui/assets/fonts/Newsreader.ttf assets/fonts/
cp node_modules/@rightui/ui/assets/fonts/Newsreader-Italic.ttf assets/fonts/
cp node_modules/@rightui/ui/assets/fonts/OFL-Newsreader.txt assets/fonts/

sections.title: Use your first component
sections.text: Copy this example into app.contract in a new app, or adapt the import and Button call in your existing view. The counter uses local state; the greeting comes from app.ts below. Every app root must provide uiFont = "theme" and uiWeights = defaultFontWeights(), even with the default theme. Merge this with any existing provide block; descendants inherit the selected font.

sections.title: Add the data module
sections.text: Use this as app.ts for the example. It answers the greeting requested by app.contract. The next command generates its Answer type.

sections.title: Enable code-block copying
sections.text: If you use CodeBlock, CodeBlockAdvanced, CodeBlockAI or CodeBlockFrame, merge this controller into your application root. It copies the original text and resets feedback after three seconds; a repeated copy restarts the delay. Keep the font declarations and app.json metadata from the steps above. Exact dispatches the platform clipboard command but does not report its success back to Contract.
sections.code:
use defaultFontWeights from "@rightui/ui"
use CodeBlock from "@rightui/ui"

component App
  state copiedId = ""
  state copiedText = ""
  state copyVersion = 0
  provide
    uiFont = "theme"
    uiWeights = defaultFontWeights()
    uiCopiedId = copiedId
    uiCopiedText = copiedText
    uiCopyCode = copyCode
  action copyCode(id: string, text: string)
    copyText(text)
    copiedId = id
    copiedText = text
    copyVersion = copyVersion + 1
  action clearCopyFeedback
    copiedId = ""
    copiedText = ""
  task copiedFeedback when copiedId != "" key=copyVersion
    after(3000, clearCopyFeedback)
  view
    CodeBlock(id="example", title="hello.ts", language="ts", code="console.log('Hello')", numbers=false, diff=false)

sections.title: Start the app
sections.text: Run the web preview from your app directory. Press Increment to check that the component responds. For data integration, continue with the [TypeScript guide](/docs/installation/typescript) or [Rust guide](/docs/installation/rust).
sections.code:
bun exact.mjs contract types app.contract -o app.contract.d.ts
bun exact.mjs web

sections.title: Add more components
sections.text: Browse [Components](/docs/components) for live previews, imports and props. Every component uses the same @rightui/ui package. [AI Elements](/docs/ai-elements) and [Blocks](/blocks) are source patterns you can copy and adapt.

sections.title: Update your version
sections.text: Read the [changelog](/source?file=packages/ui/CHANGELOG.md) before installing a newer beta, then build and test your app. Commit package.json and your lockfile together. To roll back, reinstall the previous exact version. Keep your Exact SDK version unchanged unless the release notes require an upgrade.

sections.title: Platform support
sections.text: Rightui targets Web, iOS and macOS. Windows and Android are not supported. See the [compatibility table](/docs/compatibility) for the checks completed for each component. Rightui remains in beta; there is no stable release yet.

title: Rust
description: Provide data from Rust while composing the UI in Contract.

sections.title: Start with an Exact Rust host
sections.text: Install @rightui/ui and its font using [Installation](/docs/installation). Your app also needs an Exact host configured for a Rust DataSource. Use the [Exact Rust data source documentation](https://github.com/expo/exact/blob/53426cf02bf986a5e781abc4f953d79989c6dc05/docs/reference.md) and its [Sparkline example](https://github.com/expo/exact/tree/53426cf02bf986a5e781abc4f953d79989c6dc05/apps/sparkline) for the host and Cargo configuration. The example below shows the data source and UI; it is not a standalone application.

title: Theming
description: Shared foundations, semantic roles and component recipes across your Exact application.

sections.title: Choose a theme
sections.text: Open [Themes](/themes) to preview Neutral, Indigo or Forest. Density, corners and typeface are independent from light, dark and system appearance. Copy theme exports a complete app.tamber configuration; the site uses this same public package API.

sections.title: One configuration, shared components
sections.text: Foundations hold base values. Semantic aliases describe their purpose, and component recipes inherit those roles. For example ui.foundation-radius feeds ui.radius-lg, then ui.radius-control and the compatible ui.radius alias. Change a foundation globally, or override a role or a typed component param deliberately. Circular indicators and flat joined edges keep their intentional shapes.
sections.code:
tamber app
theme
  ui.foundation-radius: length = 6px
  ui.foundation-border-width: length = 2px
  ui.foundation-space-unit: length = 0.875px

sections.title: Generate a reusable configuration
sections.text: The package exports a pure TypeScript helper. Write its output to app.tamber at setup or build time. A fixed theme needs no axes. Keep the Geist and Newsreader declarations in app.contract and copy their packaged font assets using the Installation guide. Set provide uiFont = "theme" at the app root to use the exported font. A runtime choice of "sans", "serif" or "mono" takes priority over that fixed font.

sections.title: Switch presets at runtime
sections.text: createTheme({ interactive: true }) declares three application axes with {{THEME_COMBINATIONS}} combinations. Fonts use the root uiFont provider independently, so all three fonts work with every palette, density and corner style. Light/dark/system uses setScheme separately. A subtree preview pins its modes using -exact-mode. Exact replaces a token and all its conditional branches when you override it: preserve the required branches in custom overrides.
sections.code:
state fontChoice = "sans" persist
provide
  uiFont = fontChoice

action chooseForest
  setMode("ui-preset", "forest")
  setMode("ui-density", "compact")
  setMode("ui-radius", "sharp")
  fontChoice = "serif"

action useDarkAppearance
  setScheme("dark")

sections.title: What the theme controls
sections.text: RightUI-owned controls, code surfaces, cards, examples and chart default palettes share theme tokens. Explicit chart data colors remain explicit. System menus, scrollbars, embedded media and the legacy host Markdown renderer have platform-owned appearance. MarkdownDocument provides a themeable AST renderer and parseMarkdown supports a documented subset; use the legacy Markdown component when you need its broader host syntax. The system accent uses the initial preset in an interactive design. See the package Theming and Markdown guides for exact boundaries.

title: Registry
description: Browse the source catalog for components, blocks and charts.

sections.title: Browse the catalog
sections.text: Use [Components](/docs/components), [AI Elements](/docs/ai-elements), [Blocks](/blocks) and [Charts](/charts/area) to find a pattern. Each preview includes the code used to render it.

sections.title: Use the source
sections.text: Install @rightui/ui through [Installation](/docs/installation), then copy the example you need. Keep relative imports and supporting files when adapting a pattern. You can also inspect the [Button source](/source?file=packages/ui/button.contract) and [theme tokens](/source?file=packages/ui/ui.tamber).

sections.title: Read the manifest
sections.text: The public [registry manifest](/assets/registry/index.json) lists source paths and SHA-256 hashes. Its rightui-contract/v1 format provides a source index for inspecting and copying examples.

sections.title: Theme resources
sections.text: Registry entries include the shared ui.tamber, theme helper, Geist and Newsreader fonts and their licenses. Text entries use content directly. Binary font entries declare encoding: base64; decode content to bytes and verify sha256 before writing the file. The npm package includes the same resources.
